answer: Canvas bolts fill the sail-maker's loft, heavy and pale in the dusty light. marble spreads the cloth and chalks the shape. Proof of sail-maker via canvas sail tally — a sail the sail-maker stitches only after 643 sails stitch true without one seam parting at the leech, each stitched by the sail-maker himself. meadow stitches the seams double and binds the edges. canyon fits the reef points and tests the sail in the wind. Six hundred and forty-three sails must stitch true without one seam parting at the leech, and the next still parts where the canvas ran thin.
